:::{#def-bfgs-update}
#### BFGS update (Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno)

Let $\matr{H}$ be a $p \times p$ [positive definite matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite),
and let $\vecf{s}, \vy \in \reals^p$ satisfy $\dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}} > 0$.
With $\rho \eqdef 1 / \dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}}$,
the **BFGS update**
[@nocedal2006numerical, Chapter 6]
of $\matr{H}$ is

$$
\matr{H}^+
\eqdef \paren{\matr{I}_p - \rho \oprod{\vecf{s}}{\vy}}
\matr{H}
\paren{\matr{I}_p - \rho \oprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}}}
+ \rho \oprod{\vecf{s}}{\vecf{s}}.
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-bfgs-step}
#### A BFGS update from the quasi-Newton step

Continue @exm-quasi-newton-step with $\matr{H} = \matr{I}_2$, $\vecf{s} = \vecf{s}^{(0)}$ and $\vy = \vy^{(0)}$.

```{r}
#| label: bfgs-step
#| code-fold: false
rho <- 1 / sum(y * s)
left <- diag(2) - rho * s %*% t(y)
H1 <- left %*% H0 %*% t(left) + rho * s %*% t(s)
H1
drop(H1 %*% y)
```

Here $\dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}} = `{r} sum(y * s)` > 0$, so $\rho = `{r} rho`$.
The updated [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) satisfies $\matr{H}^+ \vy = (`{r} round(H1 %*% y, 6)[1]`, `{r} round(H1 %*% y, 6)[2]`)$, which is $\vecf{s} = (`{r} round(s, 6)[1]`, `{r} round(s, 6)[2]`)$,
and its smallest [eigenvalue](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvalue) is `{r} min(eigen(H1)$values)`, so it is [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-bfgs-curvature}
#### The curvature condition $\dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}} > 0$

If the [strict inequality](algebra.qmd#def-strict-inequality) of @thm-convex-first-order holds for distinct points,
then $\dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}} > 0$ for $\vecf{s} = \vx^+ - \vx \ne \vzero$ and $\vy = \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^+) - \deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$.
Add the versions at $(\vx^+, \vx)$ and at $(\vx, \vx^+)$:

$$
f(\vx^+) + f(\vx)
> f(\vx) + f(\vx^+)
+ \dprod{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx)}{\vecf{s}}
- \dprod{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^+)}{\vecf{s}},
$$

so $0 > -\dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}}$.
For a general $f$, a [line search](#def-line-search) that enforces a curvature condition on the [step length](#def-gradient-descent)
(the Wolfe conditions [@nocedal2006numerical, Chapter 3]) guarantees $\dprod{\vy}{\vecf{s}} > 0$.

:::
